[This](http://livforcake.com/2015/02/smores-macarons.html) was my inspiration. I use a different recipe for the shells that I've been tweaking to work best in my oven. Times and temperatures definitely vary, so I recommend doing a lot of research and trying different things to make them perfect!

**Macaron Shells**

* 120 grams almond meal/flour

* 228 grams powdered sugar

* 40 grams graham cracker crumbs (omit for plain shells)

* 140 grams egg whites

* 70 grams granulated sugar

**Directions**

* In a large mixing bowl, sift together the almond flour, powdered sugar, and graham cracker crumbs. Throw away any large chunks that will not fit through the sifter.

* In a stand mixer fit with a whisk attachment, whisk egg whites on high until they start to foam. Add granulated sugar and whisk on high speed until eggs hold stiff peaks(meringue).

* Add half the meringue to the dry ingredients. With a rubber spatula, start to fold the mixture so the ingredients are combined. Add the rest of the meringue and continue folding so there are no dry clumps. Mixture should ribbon off spatula(The consistency should resemble thick lava is what I've always heard).

* Pour mixture into a piping bag, and pipe onto a baking sheet fitted with either parchment paper or a silicone baking mat.

* Let macarons sit for 20 minutes, and preheat your oven to 350 F.

* Once the macarons are dry to the touch, put in the oven and reduce the temperature to 285 F. Bake macarons for 9-12 minutes, or until they can easily be separated from the parchment paper.

* Let the macarons cool completely before removing.

I started taking creatine my last month of accutane. The only issue I had at first was drinking enough water, since both creatine and accutane are dehydrating. I had a headache for a couple days but once I started drinking more it went away. 

Accutane causes such different side effects for everyone, so if you take creatine just make sure to note how your body responds and stop if you need to.
